verb-last.name: The predicate comes last
verb-last.about: The verb, adjective or です comes at the end, before only a final particle like か; who, what, where and when all come before it.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

verb-last.short: The verb, adjective or です comes last; only a particle like か follows it: 私はコーヒーを飲みます。

topic-wa.name: は: the topic
topic-wa.about: は (said wa) after a word makes it what the sentence is about; English has no word for it.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

topic-wa.short: は (said wa) after a word makes it what the sentence is about: 私は… (as for me…).

desu.name: です: polite noun and adjective sentences
desu.about: です after a noun says what something is (学生です, I'm a student), and after an adjective makes it polite (高いです).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

desu.short: です after a noun says what something is: 学生です (I'm a student); after an adjective it's polite.

masu.name: Polite verbs in -ます
masu.about: Everyday polite verbs end in -ます, for what you do and what you will do: 行きます, I go, I'll go.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

masu.short: Polite verbs end in -ます, the same for I, you, he and she: 飲みます (drink, drinks).

masen.name: -ません: not
masen.about: -ません instead of -ます makes a polite verb negative: 行きません, I don't go.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

masen.short: -ません in place of -ます makes a verb not: 飲みません (don't drink).

mashita.name: Polite past: -ました, でした
mashita.about: -ました makes a polite verb past (-ませんでした, didn't), and です becomes でした: 雨でした, it was rainy.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

mashita.short: -ました makes a verb past, -ませんでした past and not; です becomes でした.

object-o.name: を: the object
object-o.about: を (said o) marks what the verb acts on, and comes before the verb: コーヒーを飲みます.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

object-o.short: を (said o) marks what the verb acts on: コーヒーを飲みます.

particle-ni.name: に: to, at, on
particle-ni.about: に marks where you go, where something is, and the time something happens: 七時に, at seven.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

particle-ni.short: に marks where you go, where something is, and when: 家に帰ります, テーブルの上にあります.

particle-de.name: で: at, by, with
particle-de.about: で marks where an action happens, or what you do it by or with: 駅で, at the station; バスで, by bus.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

particle-de.short: で marks where something is done, or what with: 家で飲みます (drink at home).

question-ka.name: か: questions
question-ka.about: か at the end makes a question, and the order stays the same; a question word sits where its answer would.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

question-ka.short: か at the end makes a question, the order unchanged: コーヒーですか。

possessive-no.name: の: 's and of
possessive-no.about: の joins two nouns, the owner or the kind first: 私の本, my book. On its own after a noun it means the one of: 私のです, it's mine.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

possessive-no.short: の joins two nouns, the owner first: 私の本 (my book); after a noun alone, the one of: 私のです (it's mine).

subject-ga.name: が: the subject
subject-ga.about: が marks who or what does something or is there, often something new, and the thing you like with 好きです.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

subject-ga.short: が marks who or what does something or is there, often something new: 鍵があります.

aru-iru.name: あります / います: there is, have
aru-iru.about: あります is there is for things, います for people and animals; what's there takes が, where takes に. It often means have: 時間があります.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

aru-iru.short: あります says a thing is there, います a person or animal: テーブルの上にあります; it can mean have.

adjectives.name: Adjectives
adjectives.about: い adjectives end in い and take です (高いです), and their past ends in -かったです (忙しかったです); な adjectives take な before a noun (静かな町).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

adjectives.short: い adjectives end in い and take です (高いです); な adjectives take な before a noun (静かな町).

mo.name: も: too, also
mo.about: も takes the place of は, が or を and adds too: 私も, me too.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

mo.short: も takes the place of は, が or を and adds too: 私も (me too).

want-tai.name: -たい: want to
want-tai.about: A verb's -ます stem with たいです says what you want to do: 食べたいです, I want to eat.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

want-tai.short: A verb's -ます stem with たいです says what you want to do: 飲みたいです.

te-kudasai.name: -て/-でください: please
te-kudasai.about: A verb's て form (-て or -で) with ください asks someone to do something: 待ってください, please wait.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

te-kudasai.short: A verb's て form with ください asks someone to do it: 待ってください.

mashou.name: -ましょう, -ませんか: let's
mashou.about: -ましょう says let's; -ませんか invites: 行きませんか, won't you come?

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

mashou.short: -ましょう says let's: 飲みましょう; -ませんか invites: 飲みませんか.

te-iru.name: -ています, -でいます: going on, or a state
te-iru.about: A verb's て form (-て or -で) with います says it's going on now (見ています, I'm watching) or a state that holds (住んでいます, I live).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

te-iru.short: A verb's て form with います says it's going on now: 読んでいます (am reading).

counters.name: Counters
counters.about: A number takes a counter for what's counted, after the thing: 猫が一匹, one cat; 本が二冊, two books. Some readings change: 一人 is ひとり.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

counters.short: A number takes a counter for what's counted: 一つ, 一人, 一冊.

kara-made.name: から and まで: from, to
kara-made.about: から marks where or when something starts, まで where or when it ends: 九時から五時まで, from nine to five.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

kara-made.chip: から, まで: from, to
kara-made.short: から marks where or when something starts, まで where it ends.

to-and.name: と: and, with
to-and.about: と joins nouns (パンと牛乳, bread and milk), and after a person it means with: 友達と映画を見ました, I watched a movie with a friend.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

to-and.short: と joins nouns (コーヒーとお茶) and after a person means with: 母と帰ります.

te-form.name: The て form: and then
te-form.about: A verb's て form (-て or -で) joins actions, often in the order they happen, and only the last verb shows the tense and politeness: シャワーを浴びて寝ました, I took a shower and went to bed.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

te-form.short: A verb's て form joins actions in order; only the last verb shows the tense.

ageru-kureru.name: あげる and くれる: giving
ageru-kureru.about: When I give something to someone else, it's あげます (妹に本をあげました, I gave my younger sister a book). When someone gives something to me, it's くれます (友達がお土産をくれました, a friend gave me a souvenir), and to someone in my family or group too. Who gets it takes に, when it's said.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Short name and one-line rule added in revision 2.

ageru-kureru.chip: あげる, くれる: giving
ageru-kureru.short: あげます when I give, くれます when someone gives to me.

kosoado.name: This: これ, この
kosoado.about: これ is this one near me, それ that one near you, あれ that one over there; before a noun they become この, その, あの: この本 (this book). どれ and どの ask which.

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Added in revision 2 for lessons 1–20.

kosoado.short: これ and それ stand alone (これは本です); before a noun they're この and その (この本).

potential.name: Can: できます, 読めます
potential.about: できます says can do or is possible (何ができますか, what can I do?); a verb's own can form ends in -えます or -られます: 読めます (can read), 手伝えます (can help), 食べられます (can eat).

source.note: First drafted by Lexicommons, open to correction. Added in revision 2 for lessons 1–20.

potential.short: できます says can do; a verb's can form: 読めます (can read), 手伝えます (can help).

question-word.name: Question words: who, what, where, when, why
question-word.about: だれ asks who, 何 what, どこ where, いつ when, and どうして why. The question word stays where its answer would, with か at the end. だれか and 何か mean someone and something.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 21–40, open to correction.

question-word.short: A question word stays in its answer’s place, with か at the end: 予約はいつですか. だれか means someone; 何か means something.

hoshii.name: 欲しい: wanting a thing
hoshii.about: 欲しいです says you want a thing. The thing takes が; wanting to do something instead uses a verb with たいです. Use it for your own wants, or to ask the listener about theirs.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

hoshii.short: A thing you want takes が before 欲しいです: お水が欲しいです (I want some water).

adjective-negative.name: Negative adjectives: -くない, じゃない
adjective-negative.about: い adjectives make their negative with -くないです; な adjectives take じゃないです. いい becomes よくないです. (高くありません says the same as 高くないです; these lessons use -くないです.)

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

adjective-negative.short: Change an い adjective’s final い to くない: 高くないです (いい: よくないです). A な adjective takes じゃないです: 静かじゃないです.

past-adjective.name: Past adjectives: -かったです, でした
past-adjective.about: An い adjective carries past tense in -かった, followed by です. With a な adjective, change です to でした.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

past-adjective.short: Change an い adjective’s final い to かった: 面白かったです (いい: よかったです). A な adjective takes でした: 静かでした.

to-omou.name: と思います: saying what you think
to-omou.about: The thought comes before と and 思います. A nonpast affirmative verb inside the thought uses its dictionary form. An い adjective goes directly before と. The ending 思います keeps the whole sentence polite.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

to-omou.short: Put the thought before と思います: 五時に来ると思います (I think they will come at five). 来る is the dictionary form of 来ます.

kara-because.name: から: giving a reason
kara-because.about: から after a clause gives a reason. In these polite sentences, the reason keeps ます or です. The result follows it.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

kara-because.short: Put から after the reason: 電車が止まりましたから、遅れました (I was late because the train stopped).

verb-particles.name: Choose the particle with the verb
verb-particles.about: A Japanese verb determines the particle for the person, vehicle or place connected to it. Wait for someone with を, meet someone with に, get on a vehicle with に, and mark a place you leave with を.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 41–60, open to correction.

verb-particles.short: 友達を待ちます, 友達に会います, 電車に乗ります, 家を出ます: learn the verb with the particle for that job.

noun-modify.name: Adjectives before nouns
noun-modify.about: An い adjective comes directly before the noun it describes. A な adjective needs な before that noun. Never put です between an adjective and its noun: 面白い本, 静かな部屋.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 61–80, open to correction.

noun-modify.short: Put an い adjective before its noun: 面白い本. A な adjective takes な: 静かな部屋, きれいな写真. Do not put です inside the noun phrase.

naide-kudasai.name: -ないでください: please do not
naide-kudasai.about: A verb in its negative ない form followed by でください asks someone not to do something. The negative form occurs only inside this polite request in this round.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 61–80, open to correction.

naide-kudasai.short: Use the negative form plus でください: 置かないでください (please do not put it there), 開けないでください (please do not open it).

purpose.name: Purpose: going to do something
purpose.about: The verb stem left after removing ます takes に before a motion verb such as 行きます, 来ます or 帰ります. It says the purpose of going, coming or returning. An activity noun such as 散歩 can also take に.

source.note: Written with the Japanese lessons 61–80, open to correction.

purpose.short: Remove ます, then add に and a motion verb: 飲みに行きます (go to drink), 会いに行きます (go to meet). An activity noun also works: 散歩に行きます (go for a walk).
